Definition: Designing technology so that people with disabilities can find, understand and operate it.
A device or program that helps a person with a disability use a computer, such as a screen reader or a switch.
The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the W3C's international standard for accessible web content, also used for apps.
One testable rule in WCAG, such as 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum).
How strict a WCAG success criterion is: A, AA or AAA.
A number from 1 to 21 that compares how light two colors are. Higher numbers are easier to tell apart.
A program that turns what is on the screen into speech or braille.
A device with small pins that rise and fall to show a line of braille, read by touch.
A system that follows where a person looks to move the pointer, and can click when they blink.
A simple input device, such as a large button or a sip-and-puff tube, that a person uses instead of a keyboard or mouse.
A text version of the speech and other sounds in a video or audio, shown in time with it.
